sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was effectively lowered: management explicitly stated they are in an 'investment period' with 'incremental EBITDA pressure over the next couple of quarters' and expects 'further ARPU pressure' in broadband, while also noting that one-time cash tax benefits in 2025 'will not recur' in 2026. Although the company highlighted record free cash flow and strong wireless growth, the explicit forward-looking statements point to continued near-term EBITDA and ARPU declines, with management stopping short of providing a full-year EBITDA guide and only promising 'improvement' in the back half of 2026. The cautious, investment-period framing and explicit forward pressure outweigh the positive backward-looking results, resulting in a negative sentiment score.

summary.revenue: 4Q25 revenue was $32,310 million, up 1.2% year-over-year. Full-year 2025 revenue was $123,707 million, flat year-over-year.
summary.eps: 4Q25 diluted EPS was $0.60, down 52.0% year-over-year. Adjusted EPS was $0.84, down 12.4% year-over-year. Full-year 2025 diluted EPS was $5.39, up 30.1%; Adjusted EPS was $4.31, down 0.6%.
summary.guidance: Management stated they are in an 'investment period' and expect 'incremental EBITDA pressure over the next couple of quarters' until they begin to lap investments in the second half of 2026. They expect 'further ARPU pressure' in broadband for the next couple of quarters. For 2026, they expect total capital spending to be 'relatively similar to 2025' and expect Peacock losses to 'meaningfully improve again.' They expect to convert 'the vast majority of free lines into paying relationships' in the second half of 2026. They did not provide a full-year EBITDA guide.
summary.margin: Connectivity & Platforms Adjusted EBITDA margin was 37.1% in 4Q25, down 120 bps year-over-year. Residential Connectivity & Platforms Adjusted EBITDA margin was 34.6%, down 140 bps. Business Services Connectivity Adjusted EBITDA margin was 54.2%, down 150 bps.
key_risks: Intense broadband competition, including from fiber and fixed wireless.
Increased wireless competition, particularly towards the end of the fourth quarter.
Incremental EBITDA pressure expected over the next couple of quarters due to the investment period.
Further broadband ARPU pressure expected for the next couple of quarters.
One-time cash tax benefits in 2025 will not recur in 2026.
Leverage ratios will increase slightly on the back of the Versant spin-off.
The Versant spin-off removes a significant pool of cash flow from operations.
key_opportunities: Wireless growth: 1.5 million net line additions in 2025, reaching 9.3 million total lines and surpassing 15% penetration of domestic residential broadband customers.
Theme Parks growth: Epic Universe driving higher per-cap spending and attendance; Theme Parks crossed $1 billion in quarterly EBITDA for the first time.
Peacock growth: 44 million paid subscribers, up 22% year-over-year; revenue grew 23% in 4Q25; full-year EBITDA losses improved by over $700 million.
Network leadership: ~60% of footprint transitioned to mid-split spectrum; plan to market multi-gigabit symmetrical speeds.
Business Services growth: revenue increased 6% in 4Q25, driven by enterprise solutions.
Free wireless line conversion: expect to convert the vast majority of free lines into paying relationships in the second half of 2026.
